title: Convoy TE-04, 3–4 May 1944
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · Coordinated attack group, Capt. G. E. Peterson

participants.name: PARCHE
participants.co: LCdr L. P. Ramage; pack commander Capt. G. E. Peterson aboard

paras.text: TINOSA found convoy TE-04 north of Luzon on the morning of 3 May and reported it to PARCHE and BANG; by the early hours of the 4th the three boats had attacked it in turn, and five of its six ships were gone. The boats' war patrol reports beside the escort division's record, on one GMT clock.
Japanese loss list: five ships, 30,542 GRT. Which boat sank which is still open; see the attack order in the log.
Yulin to Moji by way of Keelung, sailed 30 April with six ships; iron ore for Yawata (combinedfleet.com, secondary). Its ships are in the convoy's own record: [[convoy:te-04]].

Positions are the boats' own dead reckoning and star sights, and three navigators never quite agree, so the same convoy appears in slightly different places in each report. Lines between positions are straight; where a boat actually went in between is not recorded. Dashed outlines mark entries the report itself contradicts, kept with the reason.

BANG kept zone K (−10) and PARCHE zone I (−9); TINOSA kept zone H (−8) on station. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). On 29–30 April the target ship's own log and BANG's attack sheets agree to within one to seven minutes once both are in GMT.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (BANG 74802746, PARCHE 74828582, TINOSA 74856363). Nittatsu Maru's movement log and the 1st Surface Escort Division war diary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy lists and the 3–4 May sinking times from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.title: Attack 2
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 2 (TE-04; 4 + 2 fired; claims two AKs sunk)

outcome.note: PARCHE fired 4 + 2 from 20-48N 118-03E at 0106 I, at targets 1,850 and 2,250 yards off, saw five hits and claimed two AKs sunk, one breaking up in under two minutes. Kinrei Maru's own log has her torpedoed and sunk at 0109 I at 20-42N 118-01E: three minutes after PARCHE fired, about 6 nm south of PARCHE's position. No other boat fired near that time: TINOSA was deep from 0012 until 0234 I, and BANG's only attack that night was at 0232 I. The secondary source (J03) and JANAC credit her to BANG, JANAC as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59), which is why this is probable and not hit

PARCHE's second target "settled stern first. Sank in 10 minutes"; the secondary source's 0113 I for Daibu Maru is seven minutes after PARCHE fired, and its times for Toyohi (0008) and Kinrei Maru (0106) are within three minutes of those ships' own logs. JANAC credits Daibu (Taibu) Maru to TINOSA as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p51), whose second salvo hit an AK at 0010-53 I, an hour before. No primary record of Daibu Maru found. Possible either way, the time favouring PARCHE

events.title: Attack 3
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 3 (TE-04; 4 fired; claims one AK or AP sunk)

outcome.note: The secondary source credits PARCHE with Shoryu and Daiyoku Maru "about 0300", as does JANAC. Neither fits: by their own logs Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru sank at 0237 I at 20-56N 118-04E (J06), five minutes after BANG's Attack 5, and Shoryu Maru at 0353 I at 20-54N 118-08E (J05), four minutes after TINOSA's Attack 3; PARCHE fired nothing after 0127 I

events.title: Attack 5
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 5

outcome.note: Not BANG's. Kinrei Maru's own log has her torpedoed and sunk at 0109 I at 20-42N 118-01E, bound for Keelung (jacar:C08050104500 p30; PARCHE's Patrol 1 J08), 83 minutes before BANG's only attack that night (0232 I) and three minutes after PARCHE fired her Attack 2 (0106 I). JANAC credits BANG with Kinrei Maru, as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p3); the ship's log doesn't support it. The secondary source's 0106 I (J12) was near the log's time. Taiyoku Maru (J20, 0237 I) is the loss that fits this attack

BANG's Attack 5 (0232 I) is 28 minutes before the secondary source's "about 0300" for Shoryu and Daiyoku Marus, which it credits to PARCHE. So does JANAC: Shoryu Maru (6,475 tons) not marked probable, Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru (5,244 tons) "Submarine*", probable; both 4 May at 20-48N 118-03E (janac:4/p59; janac:6/p27) Superseded by J20 for Taiyoku Maru: J15 and J20 describe the same loss and count once; the ships' own logs put Taiyoku at 0237 I and Shoryu at 0353 I (TINOSA's Patrol 6 J04), not together at "about 0300"

Taiyoku Maru's own log: torpedoed and sank at 0237 I at 20-56N 118-04E, five minutes after BANG fired at 0232 I (0332 K) and about 5 nm from BANG's attack position (20-58N 117-59E). No other boat was firing then: PARCHE's last attack was at 0127 I and TINOSA was deep under depth charges until 0234 I (0134 H), firing next at 0349 I. Against: JANAC credits Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru to PARCHE, as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p27), and the secondary source (J15) agrees with JANAC. That credit is why this is probable, not hit. J11, J15 and this entry are one loss, counted once

events.words: Summary of attacks: 4 stern tubes at damaged AK; results unknown

events.title: Attack 5 (narrative)
events.words: Started firing 4 stern tubes on 95 port track

pairs.note: Not BANG's. Kinrei Maru's own log has her torpedoed and sunk at 0109 I at 20-42N 118-01E, bound for Keelung (jacar:C08050104500 p30; PARCHE's Patrol 1 J08), 83 minutes before BANG's only attack that night (0232 I) and three minutes after PARCHE fired her Attack 2 (0106 I). JANAC credits BANG with Kinrei Maru, as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p3); the ship's log doesn't support it. The secondary source's 0106 I (J12) was near the log's time. Taiyoku Maru (J20, 0237 I) is the loss that fits this attack

record.translation: At 0106, BANG torpedoes and sinks Kinrei Maru at 20-50N, 117-55E
record.note: Secondary source (combinedfleet.com record of Daiyoku Maru). Zone assumed I like the other Japanese records. Order there: TINOSA 0008 (Toyohi), BANG 0106 (Kinrei), TINOSA 0113 (Daibu), PARCHE about 0300 (Shoryu, Daiyoku), all near 20-50N 117-55E

intelligence.note: Times stacked by two dots near TE-04's track, about 20 nm NE of Attack 5 (20-58N 117-59E). In Tokyo time these are 47-133 minutes before BANG's 0232 I; Kinrei Maru sank 0106 I (J12, secondary). Likely TINOSA's and PARCHE's attacks
About 12 nm east of Attack 5; 112 minutes earlier. Nothing on the map at BANG's 0232 I

pairs.note: BANG's Attack 5 (0232 I) is 28 minutes before the secondary source's "about 0300" for Shoryu and Daiyoku Marus, which it credits to PARCHE. So does JANAC: Shoryu Maru (6,475 tons) not marked probable, Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru (5,244 tons) "Submarine*", probable; both 4 May at 20-48N 118-03E (janac:4/p59; janac:6/p27) Superseded by J20 for Taiyoku Maru: J15 and J20 describe the same loss and count once; the ships' own logs put Taiyoku at 0237 I and Shoryu at 0353 I (TINOSA's Patrol 6 J04), not together at "about 0300"

record.translation: At about 0300, PARCHE torpedoes and sinks Shoryu and Daiyoku (Taiyoku) Marus at 20-50N, 117-55E
record.note: Secondary source; time given as "about". Both in the May loss list (J11): Shoryu 6,475 GRT, Taiyoku 5,244 GRT. PARCHE's report has no attack after 0127 I. BANG's Attack 5 (0232 I) and TINOSA's Attack 3 (0349 I) are the attacks near 0300

intelligence.note: Times stacked by two dots near TE-04's track, about 20 nm NE of Attack 5 (20-58N 117-59E). In Tokyo time these are 47-133 minutes before BANG's 0232 I; Kinrei Maru sank 0106 I (J12, secondary). Likely TINOSA's and PARCHE's attacks
About 12 nm east of Attack 5; 112 minutes earlier. Nothing on the map at BANG's 0232 I

pairs.note: Taiyoku Maru's own log: torpedoed and sank at 0237 I at 20-56N 118-04E, five minutes after BANG fired at 0232 I (0332 K) and about 5 nm from BANG's attack position (20-58N 117-59E). No other boat was firing then: PARCHE's last attack was at 0127 I and TINOSA was deep under depth charges until 0234 I (0134 H), firing next at 0349 I. Against: JANAC credits Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru to PARCHE, as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p27), and the secondary source (J15) agrees with JANAC. That credit is why this is probable, not hit. J11, J15 and this entry are one loss, counted once

record.original: 一九.四.三〇 楡林 積荷八〇〇〇噸 船客六名 英霊四柱 基隆向航行中五月四日二時三十七分東経一一八度〇四分(p11)北緯二〇度五六分ニ於テ敵潜ノ雷撃ヲ受ケ沈没
record.translation: 30 April 1944, [from] Yulin, loaded 8,000 t, 6 passengers, the remains of four war dead. While bound for Keelung, at 0237 on 4 May, at E 118°04′ N 20°56′, torpedoed by an enemy submarine and sank
record.note: Taiyoku Maru's (大翼丸, combinedfleet's Daiyoku Maru) own movement log (designated-ship movement tables, 5th series, タ–ワ part 2; header p9). The entry runs from the foot of p10 to the top of p11. Zone not written; taken as I like the convoys' other logs. The same loss as the secondary source's J15 ("about 0300", with Shoryu Maru) and the May loss list's 大翼丸 (J11): one loss, counted once. Shoryu Maru's own log (TINOSA's Patrol 6 J04) puts her sinking at 0353 I, after TINOSA's Attack 3, so J15's pairing of the two at "about 0300" doesn't hold

intelligence.note: Times stacked by two dots near TE-04's track, about 20 nm NE of Attack 5 (20-58N 117-59E). In Tokyo time these are 47-133 minutes before BANG's 0232 I; Kinrei Maru sank 0106 I (J12, secondary). Likely TINOSA's and PARCHE's attacks
About 12 nm east of Attack 5; 112 minutes earlier. Nothing on the map at BANG's 0232 I

pairs.note: PARCHE fired 4 + 2 from 20-48N 118-03E at 0106 I, at targets 1,850 and 2,250 yards off, saw five hits and claimed two AKs sunk, one breaking up in under two minutes. Kinrei Maru's own log has her torpedoed and sunk at 0109 I at 20-42N 118-01E: three minutes after PARCHE fired, about 6 nm south of PARCHE's position. No other boat fired near that time: TINOSA was deep from 0012 until 0234 I, and BANG's only attack that night was at 0232 I. The secondary source (J03) and JANAC credit her to BANG, JANAC as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59), which is why this is probable and not hit

record.original: 一九.四.三〇 三亜 積荷鉄鉱石八、二〇〇噸便乗者三九名 / 一九.五.四 基隆向航行中五月四日〇一〇九北緯二〇度四二分東経一一八度〇一分ニ於テ敵潜ノ雷撃ヲ受ケ沈没ス
record.translation: 30 April 1944, [from] Sanya, loaded 8,200 t of iron ore, 39 passengers. 4 May 1944: while bound for Keelung, at 0109 on 4 May, at N 20°42′ E 118°01′, torpedoed by an enemy submarine and sank
record.note: Kinrei Maru's (金嶺丸) own movement log (designated-ship movement tables, 5th series, ア–ソ part 7; header p27). Handwritten in a rough hand; the minutes of latitude read 四二 (the second figure is two strokes). Zone not written; taken as I. Same reading as TINOSA's Patrol 6 J07

pairs.note: PARCHE's second target "settled stern first. Sank in 10 minutes"; the secondary source's 0113 I for Daibu Maru is seven minutes after PARCHE fired, and its times for Toyohi (0008) and Kinrei Maru (0106) are within three minutes of those ships' own logs. JANAC credits Daibu (Taibu) Maru to TINOSA as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p51), whose second salvo hit an AK at 0010-53 I, an hour before. No primary record of Daibu Maru found. Possible either way, the time favouring PARCHE

record.translation: At 0113, TINOSA torpedoes and sinks Daibu Maru at 20-50N, 117-55E
record.note: Secondary source (BANG's Patrol 1 J14); zone assumed I. No primary record of her time found

pairs.note: The secondary source credits PARCHE with Shoryu and Daiyoku Maru "about 0300", as does JANAC. Neither fits: by their own logs Taiyoku (Daiyoku) Maru sank at 0237 I at 20-56N 118-04E (J06), five minutes after BANG's Attack 5, and Shoryu Maru at 0353 I at 20-54N 118-08E (J05), four minutes after TINOSA's Attack 3; PARCHE fired nothing after 0127 I

record.translation: At about 0300, PARCHE torpedoes and sinks Shoryu and Daiyoku (Taiyoku) Marus at 20-50N, 117-55E
record.note: Secondary source (BANG's Patrol 1 J15); time given as "about". The two ships' own logs give 0353 (J05) and 0237 (J06)

pairs.note: TINOSA's first salvo, fired at 2309 H (0009 I), hit a tanker under the bridge and the bow at 2310 H (0010 I), and she sank at 20-51N 118-02E (the narrative's position of the target). Toyohi Maru's own log has her torpedoed and sunk at 0008 I at 20-51N 118-03E: one to two minutes before TINOSA's firing and hits (the two clocks need only differ by that much), and about 1 nm from the narrative's position. She was an ore carrier loaded at Yulin, not a tanker. JANAC credits Toyohi Maru (6,436 tons) to TINOSA, not marked probable: 4 May, 20-51N 118-02E (janac:4/p59; janac:6/p51). The secondary source (J03) has the same 0008 I

record.original: 昭和一九.四.二九 楡林 積荷鉱石一一、三五〇噸 / 昭和一九.五.四 内地向ケ航行中五月四日〇〇〇八北緯二〇度五一分東経一一八度三分ノ位置ニ於テ敵潜ノ雷撃ヲ受ケ沈没ス
record.translation: 29 April 1944, [from] Yulin, loaded 11,350 t of ore. 4 May 1944: while bound for the home islands, at 0008 on 4 May, at N 20°51′ E 118°3′, torpedoed by an enemy submarine and sank
record.note: Toyohi Maru's (豊日丸) own movement log (designated-ship movement tables, 5th series, タ–ワ part 4; header p52, the last ship in the part). The longitude is written 一一八度三分, without a 〇. Zone not written; taken as I like the convoy's other logs. She was an ore carrier, loaded at Yulin; TINOSA took her for a tanker

pairs.note: The second salvo hit an AK of about 6,000 tons at 2310-53 H (0010-53 I), and one torpedo hit an AK in the far column at 2311-52 H (0011-52 I); TINOSA then went deep under depth charges until 0134 H (0234 I) and didn't see either sink. Of the convoy's five losses, four now have their own logs, and none of them fits a ship hit at 0010-0012 I but Toyohi Maru (J06): Kinrei Maru sank at 0109 I (J07), 58 minutes later and 3 minutes after PARCHE fired, about 9 nm south of TINOSA's attack. That leaves Daibu Maru, timed only by the secondary source at 0113 I (J05), 61 minutes after the far-column hit and 7 minutes after PARCHE's Attack 2; JANAC credits her to TINOSA as probable ("Submarine*"; 20-54N 118-14E; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p51). A ship hit at 0011 I could have sunk an hour later, but PARCHE's second target, hit at 0106 I and seen to sink, fits the time better. Possible

record.translation: At 0113, TINOSA torpedoes and sinks Daibu Maru at 20-50N, 117-55E
record.note: Secondary source, as in BANG's Patrol 1 (its J14); zone assumed I. Daibu Maru (大武丸), 6,440 GRT, is in the May loss list (J02). No primary record of her time or position found: she is in neither the 4th nor the 5th series of the designated-ship movement tables. The secondary source's times for Toyohi (0008) and Kinrei Maru (0106) are within three minutes of those ships' own logs (J06, J07), so its 0113 may come from a record of the same kind (inferred)

pairs.note: TINOSA fired four stern tubes at 0249-31 H (0349 I), heard three hits and saw the target "merely disintegrate", at 20-55N 118-12E. Shoryu Maru's own log puts her sinking at 0353 I, four minutes later, at 20-54N 118-08E, about 4 nm away. No other boat attacked near that time: PARCHE's last attack was 0127 I and BANG's 0232 I. JANAC credits Shoryu Maru to PARCHE, not marked probable (4 May, 20-48N 118-03E; janac:4/p59; janac:6/p27), which is why this is probable and not hit. Supersedes the "possible" pairing with the secondary source's "about 0300" in BANG's Patrol 1 file

record.original: 一九.五.四 北緯二〇度五四分東経一一八度〇八分 敵潜ノ魚雷攻撃ヲ受ケ沈没(〇三.五三時)
record.translation: 4 May 1944, N 20°54′ E 118°08′, torpedoed by an enemy submarine and sank (0353)
record.note: Shoryu Maru's own movement log (designated-ship movement tables, 5th series, ア–ソ part 11; header p2, kept by the first engineer as acting master). The row before: 1944.4.30, from Sanya (三亜), loaded 9,930 t, 29 passengers. The time is in brackets at the foot of the entry, read 〇三.五三時; the last digit is small but reads as 三. Zone not written; taken as I like the convoys' other logs

te-04.plain: a six-ship Yulin–Moji convoy by way of Keelung, carrying iron ore for Yawata

ships.fate: sunk 1944-05-04 0109 I at 20-42N 118-01E, her own log (PARCHE patrol 1 J08; jacar:C08050104500 p30)
ships.note: Written 金嶺丸 among the five 沈没 (sunk) beside the テ04 track on the May chart 別表第三 (Moji–Yulin) of the 1st Surface Escort Division diary; 5947 GRT in the same diary's May loss list (p26). Iron ore for Yawata per combinedfleet (secondary); not in this record

ships.fate: sunk 1944-05-04 0353 I at 20-54N 118-08E, her own log (TINOSA patrol 6 J04; jacar:C08050104900 p4)
ships.note: Written 昌竜丸 among the five 沈没 (sunk) beside the テ04 track on the May chart 別表第三 (Moji–Yulin) of the 1st Surface Escort Division diary; 6475 GRT in the same diary's May loss list (p26). Iron ore for Yawata per combinedfleet (secondary); not in this record

ships.fate: sunk 1944-05-04 0237 I at 20-56N 118-04E, her own log (BANG patrol 1 J20; jacar:C08050105400 p10)
ships.note: Written 大翼丸 among the five 沈没 (sunk) beside the テ04 track on the May chart 別表第三 (Moji–Yulin) of the 1st Surface Escort Division diary; 5244 GRT in the same diary's May loss list (p26). Iron ore for Yawata per combinedfleet (secondary); not in this record

ships.fate: sunk 1944-05-04 0008 I at 20-51N 118-03E, her own log (TINOSA patrol 6 J06; jacar:C08050105600 p53)
ships.note: Written 豊日丸 among the five 沈没 (sunk) beside the テ04 track on the May chart 別表第三 (Moji–Yulin) of the 1st Surface Escort Division diary; 6436 GRT in the same diary's May loss list (p26). Iron ore for Yawata per combinedfleet (secondary); not in this record

Written 大武丸 among the five 沈没 (sunk) beside the テ04 track on the May chart 別表第三 (Moji–Yulin) of the 1st Surface Escort Division diary; 6440 GRT in the same diary's May loss list (p26). Iron ore for Yawata per combinedfleet (secondary); not in this record
Named by combinedfleet. The April chart's escort cell for テ04 (jacar:C08030140600 p33) is cramped; its first characters may read 海一 (CD-1), not read with confidence
Auxiliary gunboat. Named by combinedfleet only
Minelayer, joined 3 May. Named by combinedfleet only

paras.text: Yulin to Moji, leaving Yulin on 30 April 1944 with six ships (April chart). The May chart draws the northbound track with two sinking marks and lists five ships sunk: 金嶺丸 昌竜丸 大翼丸 豊日丸 大武丸; the rest of the convoy is drawn into (基隆) Keelung for supplies (補給) and on to Moji. Six ships less five sunk leaves one survivor (inferred).

The chart's time and position beside the marks are faint: read 「4日 22?9」 N2?-46 E118-?4, low confidence; not paired with any one boat's attack. BANG, PARCHE and TINOSA attacked between the evening of the 3rd and the early hours of the 4th (engagement `luzon-strait-1944`, which weighs who sank which).
**Cargo: iron ore for Yawata** per combinedfleet.com (secondary); not in the escort division's record. The escorts are combinedfleet's; the April chart's escort cell can't be read with confidence.
The retired battle page listed a sixth ship, "Yulin", from combinedfleet.com; that is the port of departure, not a ship, and is left out. The sixth ship (the survivor) is not named in the record.

words.type_attack: Night surface radar attack, using constant radar ranges and constant TBT bearings to TDC. Used 1° spread between torpedoes applied from forward aft by means of the offset knob of TDC.
words.description: One 5000-9000 ton AK or AP identified at 3400 yards as silhouette similar to page 59, 60 or 62 in O.N.I. 208-J (issue August 24, 1942). This target gave largest radar pip at greater range than two other Marus. Two destroyers, best seen with 90° angle on the bow at 4000 yards, very long and low, tapering from highest point about ¼ length from bow back to stern, believed to be UN-1 class, O.N.I. 41-42. One Maru otherwise unidentified. These ships in line at time of firing. These ships part of convoy consisting of at least six Marus and five escorts that had been scattered by previous attacks by PARCHE and TINOSA.
words.sunk: One 5000-9000 ton AK or AP. One DD.
words.determined_by: Saw and heard two hits in Maru, saw her explode in flame, saw her radar pip disappear. Heard hit in DD, saw her radar pip disappear. Was entering rain squall for protection at time of explosions and could see Maru only by fire with which she burned before she sank. Could not see DD at time of hit, but saw her pip very definitely disappear about one minute after the Maru sunk. The four ships had all been sighted on the bridge before firing, their pips were distinct and separate at time of firing. The PPI showed the very definite disappearance of the two near pips.
words.target_line: Target (Maru) Draft: 27 ft. Course: 065°T. Speed: 7.8 knots Range: 3400 yds. / (DD) Draft: 10 Ft. Course: 065°T. Speed: 7.8 knots Range: 4200 yds.
words.own_ship: Speed: 0.5 knots Course: 340°T. Depth: Surface Angle: 0° (at firing)
words.remarks: Target group was lined up as shown in below sketch at time of firing. ... The time of hits were recorded as 2m 15s, 2m 21s, and 2m 45s after first torpedo was fired. The time of run, and plot of data, indicates that the first torpedo fired hit the DD, and the second and third torpedoes hit the AP.
words.note: The sheet types two targets, the Maru at 3400 yards and a DD at 4200, on one course and speed; attacks.csv gives the Maru's draft and range, the target the description names and the point of aim. The remarks conclude from the run times that the first torpedo (tube 9) hit the DD and the second and third the AP, though the table types no separate solution for the DD. The description calls the target an AK or AP, the remarks an AP. The sketch (p26, drawn by hand) shows AK, DD, DD and AP in line.

words.type_attack: Night surface attack on 6 ship convoy. Commenced approach from position 15,000 yards on starboard flank. Shortly thereafter convoy made a 90 degree change of course, going from a line to column formation. Crossed ahead of column regaining position on starboard bow then swung in for straight bow shots on 80 S track. Fired four torpedoes at leading ship, range 1900 yards, using radar ranges, TBT bearings, and one degree divergent spread. Then swung left to close second ship and then right for 80 S track. Fired two torpedoes at second ship, range 2200 yards. Ranges, bearings, and spread as before. Observed 3 hits on first target and 2 hits on second.
words.description: (1) Heavily loaded AK with long straight bow, split superstructure, MFM, slim stack similar to RYUYO MARU. (2) Heavily loaded AK, MFM, slightly raised bow, smooth deckline, split superstructure, slim stack similar to GENOA MARU.
words.sunk: (1) AK similar to RYUYO MARU. (2) AK similar to GENOA MARU.
words.determined_by: (1) 3 hits amidships, broke back, blew up and sank in less than 2 minutes. (2) 2 hits just abaft stack, settled stern first. Sank in 10 minutes.
words.target_line: Target Draft (1) 25' (2) 29' Course 030° T 030° T Speed 9½ kts 9½ kts Range 1850 yds 2250 yds (at firing)
words.own_ship: Speed 15 knots Course 286-289 T Depth Surface Angle 90-80 S (at firing)
words.spread: 1 R, 0, 1 L, 2 L, 1 L, 0 (one per torpedo, tubes 1 to 6)
words.torpedo_detail: Tube 1 Mark 23, tubes 2-4 Mark 14-3A, tubes 5-6 Mark 23; exploders 6-1A (tubes 1-4) and 6-4 (tubes 5-6); actuation set and actual Contact; warheads 16 (tubes 1-4) and 16-1 (tubes 5-6); TPX.
words.note: Tubes 1-4 typed 95 S track; own course 286-289 + gyro 002½-003 against target course 030 gives 81.5-82S, which agrees with the sheet's own words ("straight bow shots on 80 S track") and its angle on the bow (90-80 S), not with 95 S. Tubes 5 and 6 (83 S, 81 S) agree with the arithmetic. Kept as typed. Ranges: the target line types 1850 and 2250 yds, the type-of-attack words 1900 and 2200 yards; attacks.csv holds the target line's. Tubes 1-4 at the leading ship (target 1), 5-6 at the second (target 2), as the words say. Tube 6's depth set is typed 6 followed by a mark that is not clearly an apostrophe (it could be read 6½): written 6?. Firing intervals typed 0, 8, 8, 8 then 0, 8: between torpedoes, restarting for the second target.

words.type_attack: Night surface attack directly following attack No. 2 on third ship in same convoy. Maneuvered on various courses and at various speeds to obtain favorable track on target which was zigging radically. Finally steadied on course 090 T and fired 4 torpedoes on 110-120 Port track at 1600 yards with one degree divergent spread. Second and third torpedoes hit. Target appeared to be turning slowly away increasing track during the firing.
words.description: Large AK or AP, MKFKM, well decks fore and aft, composite superstructure; 3 decks, tall stack, similar to HAKONE MARU.
words.sunk: AK or AP similar to HAKONE MARU.
words.determined_by: 2 hits, one amidships and one aft blowing out after mast. Ship settled by the stern, listed heavily to port, deck awash, fires out and disappeared from radar at 6000 yards.
words.target_line: Darget Draft 29' Course 020° T Speed 9 knts Range 1675 (at firing)
words.own_ship: Speed 15 kts Course 090° T Depth Surface Angle 110° P (at firing)
words.torpedo_detail: Tube 1 Mark 14-3 A, tubes 2-4 Mark 23; exploders 6-4; actuation set and actual Contact; warheads 16-1; TPX.
words.note: Typed tracks 110P-113P are 5-6° narrower than own course 090 + gyro against target course 020 gives (116P-119P); the words say the target was turning away, increasing the track, during the firing, and give "110-120 Port track". Kept as typed. Range: the target line types 1675, the words "at 1600 yards".

words.narrative: 23-09-16(H) With range of 1,600 yards, fired 3 torpedoes from bow tubes on 105 starboard track, with 011° gyro for first torpedo, 4° spread. 23-09-52(H) With quick set-up, started firing 3 torpedoes at medium sized AK astern of Tanker. Fired on 90 starboard track about 1,500 yards range with 334° gyro. 23-10-23(H) Observed first hit in Tanker under her bridge followed by a second hit under her bow. This should have been first and second torpedoes, number three apparently missed ahead. 23-10-43(H) One hit heard but did not see it, as was watching Tanker go down. ... 23-10-53(H) Hit in AK, unidentified ship of about 6,000 tons. 23-11-52(H) Hit in AK in far column. This torpedo had missed ahead of target we were shooting at.
words.basis: Which rows had which of the table's tracks, gyros and drafts from the narrative, rg367-74856363/p15: track 105S and draft 29 (the tanker's) on the first three rows, 92S and 18 (an AK's) on the last three; gyro 011 on the first row and 333 on the fourth (the first of each salvo; the others' gyros are not given); hit on the first two rows. The values themselves, and the rest, from the summary table, p26.
words.note: The table types two tracks (105S above 92S), two gyro angles (011 above 333) and three drafts (29' 18' 18'). The narrative fires two salvos of three: at the tanker on 105 starboard track, 011° gyro for the first torpedo, and at the AK astern of her on 90 starboard track with 334° gyro. So 105S and 011 are the first salvo's, and 92S and 333 the second's; the CSV keeps the table's 92S and 333 where the narrative types 90 and 334. The table's one range (1,600) is the first salvo's; the narrative gives the second "about 1,500 yards". Which of the second salvo's torpedoes hit is not said: the narrative hears one hit at 23-10-43, a hit in the AK at 23-10-53, and a hit at 23-11-52 in an AK in the far column from a torpedo that "had missed ahead of target we were shooting at" (perhaps the first salvo's third, which "apparently missed ahead" of the tanker; the narrative doesn't say). The third row's hit and the second salvo's are left blank; the table claims 5 hits. The sunk tonnage is typed "10,000" with a mark after it (perhaps a struck-over or hand-added character). The narrative fires at 23-09-16 H on 3 May (1509 GCT) with the tanker sinking at 20-51N 118-02E, against this table's 0835 and 20-27N 118-55.5E (positions.csv); the table's time is kept.

words.narrative: 0244 (H) Range 3,000 yards, slowed to 1/3 speed and swung hard left to bring stern tubes to bear. ... Picked up target from bridge and used TBT bearings. 0247 (H) Stopped and waited for favorable gyro angles. 02-49-31(H) Started firing 4 stern tubes on 103° starboard track, 3,250 yards torpedo run using a 4° spread, first gyro angle 171°. 02-51-57(H) First of three hits. These hits were observed from the bridge: first aft of bridge, second hit under bridge, third hit in bow. ... with the third hit she merely disintegrated.
words.basis: own_depth Surface from the narrative (target picked up from the bridge, TBT bearings), rg367-74856363/p17; the rest from the summary table, p26.
words.note: The narrative's track (103° starboard) and spread (4°) agree with the table. It disagrees on the gyro: "first gyro angle 171°" against the table's 006.5 (typed with a faint point), which the CSV keeps; and on the run, 3,250 yards against the table's range of 3,200. She was stopped when she fired (0247 H, "Stopped and waited for favorable gyro angles"); own_speed is left blank, as the narrative types no figure. The narrative counts three hits, the table 4; which torpedoes hit is not said, so hit is blank. The narrative fires at 02-49-31 H on 4 May (1849 GCT 3 May), an hour before this table's 1952; the table's time is kept.

words.narrative: 0358 (H) Started in for another attack. ... came in on her starboard quarter for a bow tube shot ... Found gyro setting forward to be grounded and would not match. Trouble lights on TDC; so used Mark 8 angle solver set-up. 04-09-13(H) Fired tubes 1, 2, 3 and 4 with TBT bearings, range 3,000 yards, 160 starboard track, target now making only 6 knots, probably the AK we had previously damaged. Turned away at 20 knots ... Not able to observe results, but believe torpedoes missed ahead. 0414 (H) Two explosions sounded like torpedo hits but run was too long to have hit our target. Only explanation is that they could have hit some ship beyond our target.
